data.name: Irmine
data.gender_notes: Irmine is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Irmine is derived from the Greek word 'irmenos', meaning 'fair' or 'beautiful'. In Christian tradition, this name is associated with the virtue of humility and the gentleness of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The name Irmine carries the meaning “Fair, beautiful, gentle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Irmine usually hope their child will grow to embody fair, beautiful, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner beauty and grace.
data.etymology: Irmine belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair, beautiful, gentle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Irmine total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name Irmine has a long history, with origins in the ancient Greek language. Throughout the centuries, it has been embraced by various cultures. In the Middle Ages, Irmine was a popular name among the nobility, reflecting the beauty and elegance often attributed to the aristocracy
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Irmine holds deeper meaning beyond its etymology. It is believed to represent the humility and inner beauty that is valued in the spiritual journey. Consistent with the values of the Christian faith, Irmine can serve as a reminder of the importance of living a virtuous life, embodying humility and seeking inner beauty – just as praised in the teachings of Jesus and the example of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
data.spiritual_symbolism: As a name associated with Saint Irmine of Reims, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
